## Base Options

Input sources, output paths, and schema version handling.

- `--http-backend`: Select the HTTP client backend. 'auto' (default) selects stable HTTPX when its client module is installed and only selects experimental HTTPX2 when that module is absent. 'httpx' and 'httpx2' require that exact backend. Explicit selections and paired dependency errors do not fall back. Choices: `auto`, `httpx`, `httpx2`.
- `--input`: Input file/directory (default: stdin)
- `--input-file-type`: Input file type (default: auto). Use 'jsonschema', 'openapi', 'asyncapi', 'graphql', 'mcp-tools', 'xmlschema', 'protobuf', or 'avro' for schema definitions. Use 'json', 'yaml', or 'csv' for raw sample data to infer a schema automatically. Choices: `auto`, `openapi`, `asyncapi`, `jsonschema`, `mcp-tools`, `xmlschema`, `protobuf`, `avro`, `json`, `yaml`, `dict`, `csv`, `graphql`.
- `--external-ref-mapping`: Map external $ref file paths to Python import packages instead of generating duplicate classes. Accepts one or more mappings after a single flag. Format: "path/to/schema.yaml=mypackage.models". When a $ref points to a mapped file, an import statement is generated instead of a class definition.
- `--output`: Output file (default: stdout)
- `--emit-model-metadata`: Write a separate JSON map from generated models and fields to the JSON Pointer locations of their source schemas; module and class name identify a model.
- `--preset`: Apply an immutable built-in option preset. Preset names include the target Python version so generated syntax is pinned. - `--url`: Input file URL. `--input` is ignored when `--url` is used. For HTTP(S), datamodel-code-generator[http] remains the stable HTTPX backend and is not deprecated, while datamodel-code-generator[httpx2] is experimental. The default --http-backend auto policy selects stable HTTPX when its client module is installed and selects HTTPX2 only when that module is absent. Select --http-backend httpx2 to require the experimental backend. Explicit selections and paired dependency errors do not fall back.
- `--input-model`: Python import path or file path to a Pydantic v2 model or schema dict (e.g., 'mypackage.module:ClassName', './models.py:ClassName', or 'mypackage.schemas:SCHEMA_DICT'). Can be specified multiple times for related models with inheritance. For dict input, --input-file-type is required. Cannot be used with --input or --url.
- `--input-model-ref-strategy`: Strategy for referenced types in --input-model. 'regenerate-all': Regenerate all types. 'reuse-foreign': Reuse types from different families (Enum, etc.), regenerate same-family. 'reuse-all': Reuse all referenced types via import. If not specified, defaults to regenerate-all behavior. Choices: `regenerate-all`, `reuse-foreign`, `reuse-all`.
- `--read-input-model-dataclass-fields-by-alias`: With --input-model, read the fields of a Pydantic dataclass by their aliases, as those of a model, so a field with an alias keeps its Python type (deque[int], frozenset[str], ...) like one without; without it an aliased field of a Pydantic dataclass takes the type its JSON Schema spells (list[int]), as in 0.89.0
- `--no-read-input-model-dataclass-fields-by-alias`: With --input-model, read the fields of a Pydantic dataclass by their aliases, as those of a model, so a field with an alias keeps its Python type (deque[int], frozenset[str], ...) like one without; without it an aliased field of a Pydantic dataclass takes the type its JSON Schema spells (list[int]), as in 0.89.0
- `--reuse-every-reached-input-model-type`: With --input-model-ref-strategy reuse-all or reuse-foreign, reach the types to reuse through the fields of every model kind, dataclasses, TypedDicts and msgspec Structs too, and import a type that the Python type of a field already imports instead of writing an unused copy of it; without it reuse descends through Pydantic models only and such a copy is written (ItemModel beside Mapping[str, Item]), as in 0.89.0
- `--no-reuse-every-reached-input-model-type`: With --input-model-ref-strategy reuse-all or reuse-foreign, reach the types to reuse through the fields of every model kind, dataclasses, TypedDicts and msgspec Structs too, and import a type that the Python type of a field already imports instead of writing an unused copy of it; without it reuse descends through Pydantic models only and such a copy is written (ItemModel beside Mapping[str, Item]), as in 0.89.0
- `--encoding`: The encoding of input and output (default: utf-8)
- `--schema-version`: Schema version. Valid values depend on input type: JsonSchema: auto, draft-04, draft-06, draft-07, 2019-09, 2020-12. OpenAPI: auto, 3.0, 3.1, 3.2. AsyncAPI: auto, 2.0, 3.0. XMLSchema: auto, 1.0, 1.1. Protobuf: auto, proto2, proto3, 2023. (default: auto - detected from $schema, openapi/asyncapi field, XML Schema versioning attributes, or Protobuf syntax/edition)
- `--schema-version-mode`: Schema version validation mode. 'lenient': accept all features regardless of version (default). 'strict': warn on features outside declared/detected version. Choices: `lenient`, `strict`.
- `--read-schema-version-per-document`: Read each document by the schema version it declares ($schema, or the openapi or asyncapi field); a referenced document that declares none takes the version of the document whose reference loads it. The keywords beside a $ref and the features of the version (const, prefixItems, $id, $defs) then apply as each document's version says: a 2020-12 file of a directory read after a draft-07 one keeps the maximum beside an allOf $ref, an OpenAPI 3.1 document reads $ref siblings as JSON Schema 2020-12 does, and a draft-07 document sets no property-count rule for a minProperties beside an allOf $ref. Without it the version of the document parsed first applies to every document, as in 0.88.0. An explicit --schema-version gives every document its version; the schema validators then read an OpenAPI or AsyncAPI document by it only with the option, else as draft 7.
- `--no-read-schema-version-per-document`: Read each document by the schema version it declares ($schema, or the openapi or asyncapi field); a referenced document that declares none takes the version of the document whose reference loads it. The keywords beside a $ref and the features of the version (const, prefixItems, $id, $defs) then apply as each document's version says: a 2020-12 file of a directory read after a draft-07 one keeps the maximum beside an allOf $ref, an OpenAPI 3.1 document reads $ref siblings as JSON Schema 2020-12 does, and a draft-07 document sets no property-count rule for a minProperties beside an allOf $ref. Without it the version of the document parsed first applies to every document, as in 0.88.0. An explicit --schema-version gives every document its version; the schema validators then read an OpenAPI or AsyncAPI document by it only with the option, else as draft 7.
- `--read-escaped-ref-pointers`: Read the ~0 and ~1 escapes and the percent-encoded octets of a $ref JSON pointer as the characters they encode, as JSON Pointer and URI fragments do, so #/$defs/a~1b, and #/$defs/Foo Bar written with its space percent-encoded, name the models of the definitions a/b and Foo Bar; without it such a reference gets a copy of its target named after the escaped text (A1b, Foo20Bar), as in 0.89.0.
- `--no-read-escaped-ref-pointers`: Read the ~0 and ~1 escapes and the percent-encoded octets of a $ref JSON pointer as the characters they encode, as JSON Pointer and URI fragments do, so #/$defs/a~1b, and #/$defs/Foo Bar written with its space percent-encoded, name the models of the definitions a/b and Foo Bar; without it such a reference gets a copy of its target named after the escaped text (A1b, Foo20Bar), as in 0.89.0.
- `--read-dynamic-anchors-in-document-order`: Resolve a plain-name $dynamicRef that its dynamic scope does not bind from the $dynamicAnchors its document declares, the first in document order when several declare the name, and a $ref or $dynamicRef to a plain name several schemas of a document declare to the first of them; without it the $dynamicRef takes the first anchor the parse has met, so the answer depends on the order of the schemas, and the $ref the last declaration, as in 0.89.0.
- `--no-read-dynamic-anchors-in-document-order`: Resolve a plain-name $dynamicRef that its dynamic scope does not bind from the $dynamicAnchors its document declares, the first in document order when several declare the name, and a $ref or $dynamicRef to a plain name several schemas of a document declare to the first of them; without it the $dynamicRef takes the first anchor the parse has met, so the answer depends on the order of the schemas, and the $ref the last declaration, as in 0.89.0.
- `--ignore-ref-siblings-by-schema-version`: Read a $ref as its target alone where the schema version ignores the keywords beside it (JSON Schema draft 4, 6 and 7, OpenAPI 3.0, AsyncAPI 2), as those versions specify: a $ref with a sibling format: binary takes the referenced type instead of bytes, a sibling uniqueItems makes no set, and a sibling description or default is left out too. Versions that apply the keywords beside a $ref (2019-09 and later, OpenAPI 3.1 and later, AsyncAPI 3) read them as before. Without it the keywords beside such a $ref overlay its target, as in 0.88.0. The version is the one --read-schema-version-per-document reads, else that of the document parsed.
- `--no-ignore-ref-siblings-by-schema-version`: Read a $ref as its target alone where the schema version ignores the keywords beside it (JSON Schema draft 4, 6 and 7, OpenAPI 3.0, AsyncAPI 2), as those versions specify: a $ref with a sibling format: binary takes the referenced type instead of bytes, a sibling uniqueItems makes no set, and a sibling description or default is left out too. Versions that apply the keywords beside a $ref (2019-09 and later, OpenAPI 3.1 and later, AsyncAPI 3) read them as before. Without it the keywords beside such a $ref overlay its target, as in 0.88.0. The version is the one --read-schema-version-per-document reads, else that of the document parsed.

## Typing Customization

Type annotation, import, and primitive type behavior.

- `--use-pendulum`: use pendulum instead of datetime
- `--use-standard-primitive-types`: Use Python standard library types for string formats (UUID, IPv4Address, etc.) instead of str. Affects dataclass, msgspec, TypedDict output. Pydantic already uses these types by default.
- `--no-use-standard-primitive-types`: Use Python standard library types for string formats (UUID, IPv4Address, etc.) instead of str. Affects dataclass, msgspec, TypedDict output. Pydantic already uses these types by default.
- `--output-datetime-class`: Choose Datetime class between AwareDatetime, NaiveDatetime, PastDatetime, FutureDatetime or datetime. Each output model has its default mapping (for example pydantic: datetime, dataclass: str, ...) Choices: `datetime`, `AwareDatetime`, `NaiveDatetime`, `PastDatetime`, `FutureDatetime`.
- `--output-date-class`: Choose Date class between PastDate, FutureDate or date. (Pydantic v2 only) Each output model has its default mapping. Choices: `date`, `PastDate`, `FutureDate`.
- `--enum-field-as-literal`: Parse enum field as literal. all: all enum field type are Literal. one: field type is Literal when an enum has only one possible value. none: always use Enum class (never convert to Literal) Choices: `all`, `one`, `none`.
- `--enum-field-as-literal-map`: Per-field override for enum/literal generation (JSON or JSON file path). Format: JSON object mapping field names to 'literal' or 'enum'. Example: '{"status": "literal", "priority": "enum"}'. Overrides --enum-field-as-literal for matched fields.
- `--ignore-enum-constraints`: Ignore enum constraints and use the base type (e.g., str, int) instead of generating Enum classes
- `--use-single-value-enum-as-const`: Treat `enum` with a single value as `const` with that value, which JSON Schema defines as equal: oneOf/anyOf branches such as {"type": "string", "enum": ["low"]} merge into one Enum when there are two or more and all hold values of one JSON type, otherwise each branch is typed as written, and a schema with one enum value is typed Literal[...] instead of a one-member Enum, except one with `nullable: true` and a value other than null, which is read as written
- `--no-use-single-value-enum-as-const`: Treat `enum` with a single value as `const` with that value, which JSON Schema defines as equal: oneOf/anyOf branches such as {"type": "string", "enum": ["low"]} merge into one Enum when there are two or more and all hold values of one JSON type, otherwise each branch is typed as written, and a schema with one enum value is typed Literal[...] instead of a one-member Enum, except one with `nullable: true` and a value other than null, which is read as written
- `--read-const-beside-enum`: Read a `const` beside an `enum` as JSON Schema does: a value whose schema names the enum is typed by the const that narrows it (`Literal[Enum.member]`, a Literal or None) instead of the enum class that lists the values the const excludes, and under --use-single-value-enum-as-const an `enum` that admits its `const` is read as that `const` instead of an Enum, except one with `nullable: true` and a value other than null
- `--no-read-const-beside-enum`: Read a `const` beside an `enum` as JSON Schema does: a value whose schema names the enum is typed by the const that narrows it (`Literal[Enum.member]`, a Literal or None) instead of the enum class that lists the values the const excludes, and under --use-single-value-enum-as-const an `enum` that admits its `const` is read as that `const` instead of an Enum, except one with `nullable: true` and a value other than null
- `--filter-literal-values`: Keep only the values of a `const` or an `enum` that meet the `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, bound and `multipleOf` constraints beside them in its `Literal` or Enum, as JSON Schema validates them; a schema none of whose values meets them stays as written with a warning
- `--no-filter-literal-values`: Keep only the values of a `const` or an `enum` that meet the `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, bound and `multipleOf` constraints beside them in its `Literal` or Enum, as JSON Schema validates them; a schema none of whose values meets them stays as written with a warning
- `--intersect-allof-keywords`: Combine the keywords of every part of an `allOf`, of a `$ref` with sibling keywords and of an inherited property override, as JSON Schema validates them: the tightest bounds, the `enum` values every part admits, the `type` every part admits, the conjunction of the `pattern`s, no null beside a `type` that excludes it, and the constraints of the root, item and map value positions of an `allOf`. Without it, the keyword of the last part wins where the parts disagree
- `--no-intersect-allof-keywords`: Combine the keywords of every part of an `allOf`, of a `$ref` with sibling keywords and of an inherited property override, as JSON Schema validates them: the tightest bounds, the `enum` values every part admits, the `type` every part admits, the conjunction of the `pattern`s, no null beside a `type` that excludes it, and the constraints of the root, item and map value positions of an `allOf`. Without it, the keyword of the last part wins where the parts disagree
- `--intersect-combined-schema-keywords`: Combine the keywords of every part of a combined schema as JSON Schema validates them, as --intersect-allof-keywords does (this option turns it on), and also: the keywords beside an `anyOf` or `oneOf` in each branch, the `properties` an inherited property override merges name by name, an override that narrows the inherited `type` (such as to `null`), the length of an inherited closed tuple under --allof-merge-mode none, the `$ref` siblings of an `allOf` member where the dialect reads them, an `allOf` member that names a `$ref` alias, the null branch of an `allOf` member's `anyOf` or `oneOf`, the `required` names an `allOf` adds to the one model it names at a field, an item or a branch, and no `enum` value that the merged `type` rejects. Without it these keep the output of 0.88.0
- `--no-intersect-combined-schema-keywords`: Combine the keywords of every part of a combined schema as JSON Schema validates them, as --intersect-allof-keywords does (this option turns it on), and also: the keywords beside an `anyOf` or `oneOf` in each branch, the `properties` an inherited property override merges name by name, an override that narrows the inherited `type` (such as to `null`), the length of an inherited closed tuple under --allof-merge-mode none, the `$ref` siblings of an `allOf` member where the dialect reads them, an `allOf` member that names a `$ref` alias, the null branch of an `allOf` member's `anyOf` or `oneOf`, the `required` names an `allOf` adds to the one model it names at a field, an item or a branch, and no `enum` value that the merged `type` rejects. Without it these keep the output of 0.88.0
- `--distribute-allof-over-unions`: Read an `allOf` with the `anyOf` and `oneOf` it holds or sits beside as JSON Schema validates them: an `allOf` of several is one union variant per combination of one branch of each, also through a `$ref` member that names an `allOf` over a union, a `$ref` branch takes the `allOf` members beside its `anyOf` or `oneOf`, which an inline branch already takes, and the value keywords beside it where it names no object, and an OpenAPI request or response body with an `allOf` beside an `anyOf` or `oneOf` is that union as a schema of the components is; the value branches of those unions are read at a field and beside object branches too. Without it the branches of every `anyOf` and `oneOf` of an `allOf` join one union (the inline branches of a second replacing those of the first), a `$ref` member naming an `allOf` over a union is dropped, a `$ref` branch takes only the `properties` and `required` beside it, a body drops the union, and value branches are read only where the `allOf` would be a model without fields, as in 0.89.0
- `--no-distribute-allof-over-unions`: Read an `allOf` with the `anyOf` and `oneOf` it holds or sits beside as JSON Schema validates them: an `allOf` of several is one union variant per combination of one branch of each, also through a `$ref` member that names an `allOf` over a union, a `$ref` branch takes the `allOf` members beside its `anyOf` or `oneOf`, which an inline branch already takes, and the value keywords beside it where it names no object, and an OpenAPI request or response body with an `allOf` beside an `anyOf` or `oneOf` is that union as a schema of the components is; the value branches of those unions are read at a field and beside object branches too. Without it the branches of every `anyOf` and `oneOf` of an `allOf` join one union (the inline branches of a second replacing those of the first), a `$ref` member naming an `allOf` over a union is dropped, a `$ref` branch takes only the `properties` and `required` beside it, a body drops the union, and value branches are read only where the `allOf` would be a model without fields, as in 0.89.0
- `--read-allof-parents-in-mro-order`: Read the allOf parents of every inherited schema in the order of the class bases (the MRO), so a property that several bases declare takes the nearer base's constraints and description, as the class does, also where an allOf lists a base before its own descendant (allOf: [A, B] with B = allOf: [A, ...]); without it the parents of an inner allOf are read in document order and the property can take the farther base's looser constraints, as in 0.90.0
- `--no-read-allof-parents-in-mro-order`: Read the allOf parents of every inherited schema in the order of the class bases (the MRO), so a property that several bases declare takes the nearer base's constraints and description, as the class does, also where an allOf lists a base before its own descendant (allOf: [A, B] with B = allOf: [A, ...]); without it the parents of an inner allOf are read in document order and the property can take the farther base's looser constraints, as in 0.90.0
- `--strict-types`: Use strict types Choices: `str`, `bytes`, `int`, `float`, `bool`.
- `--use-annotated`: Use typing.Annotated for Field(). Also, `--field-constraints` option will be enabled. Will become default for Pydantic v2 in a future version.
- `--no-use-annotated`: Use typing.Annotated for Field(). Also, `--field-constraints` option will be enabled. Will become default for Pydantic v2 in a future version.
- `--use-generic-container-types`: Use generic container types for type hinting (typing.Sequence, typing.Mapping). If `--use-standard-collections` option is set, then import from collections.abc instead of typing
- `--use-non-positive-negative-number-constrained-types`: Use the Non{Positive,Negative}{FloatInt} types instead of the corresponding con* constrained types.
- `--use-decimal-for-multiple-of`: Use condecimal instead of confloat for float/number fields with multipleOf constraint (Pydantic only). Avoids floating-point precision issues in validation.
- `--use-decimal-in-field-forms`: Under --use-decimal-for-multiple-of, also write Decimal for a number with multipleOf in the field forms (--field-constraints, --use-annotated), with the constraints in Field(), and make the Decimal strict under --strict-types float (Pydantic only)
- `--no-use-decimal-in-field-forms`: Under --use-decimal-for-multiple-of, also write Decimal for a number with multipleOf in the field forms (--field-constraints, --use-annotated), with the constraints in Field(), and make the Decimal strict under --strict-types float (Pydantic only)
- `--use-encoded-str-for-constrained-base64`: Write a format: byte string with pattern, minLength or maxLength in the field forms (--field-constraints, --use-annotated) as Annotated[str, Field(...), EncodedStr(encoder=Base64Encoder)], so Pydantic 2.10 or later checks the constraints on the base64 text, as the schema does; without it Annotated[Base64Str, Field(...)] and an optional Base64Str with Field(...) check them on the decoded text, as in 0.88.0 (Pydantic v2 only)
- `--no-use-encoded-str-for-constrained-base64`: Write a format: byte string with pattern, minLength or maxLength in the field forms (--field-constraints, --use-annotated) as Annotated[str, Field(...), EncodedStr(encoder=Base64Encoder)], so Pydantic 2.10 or later checks the constraints on the base64 text, as the schema does; without it Annotated[Base64Str, Field(...)] and an optional Base64Str with Field(...) check them on the decoded text, as in 0.88.0 (Pydantic v2 only)
- `--use-standard-collections`: Use standard collections for type hinting (list, dict). Default: enabled
- `--no-use-standard-collections`: Use standard collections for type hinting (list, dict). Default: enabled
- `--use-object-type`: Use object instead of Any for unspecified JSON Schema object and array values
- `--no-use-object-type`: Use object instead of Any for unspecified JSON Schema object and array values
- `--use-typed-nullable-map-values`: Type the values of nullable maps, schemas whose type array lists object alone or with null, such as [object, null] or [object], with additionalProperties, as their schema says, with a model for object values. Without it the 0.83.0 form is kept, dict[str, Any] | None, or dict[str, Any] without null.
- `--no-use-typed-nullable-map-values`: Type the values of nullable maps, schemas whose type array lists object alone or with null, such as [object, null] or [object], with additionalProperties, as their schema says, with a model for object values. Without it the 0.83.0 form is kept, dict[str, Any] | None, or dict[str, Any] without null.
- `--use-typed-map-values-beside-other-types`: With --use-typed-nullable-map-values, also type the map values of type arrays that list object beside other types, such as [object, string], as dict[str, int] | str instead of dict[str, Any] | str
- `--no-use-typed-map-values-beside-other-types`: With --use-typed-nullable-map-values, also type the map values of type arrays that list object beside other types, such as [object, string], as dict[str, int] | str instead of dict[str, Any] | str
- `--read-unevaluated-properties`: Read a schema-valued unevaluatedProperties as additionalProperties where no applicator evaluates the object in place, so it types the extra keys of a model and makes an object without properties a map
- `--no-read-unevaluated-properties`: Read a schema-valued unevaluatedProperties as additionalProperties where no applicator evaluates the object in place, so it types the extra keys of a model and makes an object without properties a map
- `--use-single-dict-for-object-maps`: Type an object map, an object without properties whose keys patternProperties or propertyNames constrain, as one dict whose keys are those of every key class and whose value is the union of their values, beside the null and the other types of its type array
- `--no-use-single-dict-for-object-maps`: Type an object map, an object without properties whose keys patternProperties or propertyNames constrain, as one dict whose keys are those of every key class and whose value is the union of their values, beside the null and the other types of its type array
- `--use-specialized-enum`: Use specialized Enum class (StrEnum, IntEnum). Requires --target-python-version 3.11+
- `--no-use-specialized-enum`: Use specialized Enum class (StrEnum, IntEnum). Requires --target-python-version 3.11+
- `--keep-enum-member-values`: Write an enum as a plain Enum where the value base of --use-specialized-enum or --use-subclass-enum would change a member value, such as 2.5 in an IntEnum; without it the base follows the schema type, as in 0.86.0
- `--no-keep-enum-member-values`: Write an enum as a plain Enum where the value base of --use-specialized-enum or --use-subclass-enum would change a member value, such as 2.5 in an IntEnum; without it the base follows the schema type, as in 0.86.0
- `--use-union-operator`: Use | operator for Union type (PEP 604). Default: enabled
- `--no-use-union-operator`: Use | operator for Union type (PEP 604). Default: enabled
- `--use-unique-items-as-set`: define field type as `set` when the field attribute has `uniqueItems`
- `--no-use-unique-items-as-set`: define field type as `set` when the field attribute has `uniqueItems`
- `--use-unique-items-as-set-by-value`: Under --use-unique-items-as-set, decide each set once the item types are final (after --collapse-root-models, --type-overrides and every module) and write a set only where every value of its items hashes by value (scalars, enums, tuples and frozen sets of them, frozen models); an array of models that hash only by identity, of Any or of containers stays a list. Deduplication and --reuse-model also keep apart models whose arrays differ in uniqueItems; without it the sets are decided before root models collapse, set item models hash by identity and such models merge, as in 0.89.0
- `--no-use-unique-items-as-set-by-value`: Under --use-unique-items-as-set, decide each set once the item types are final (after --collapse-root-models, --type-overrides and every module) and write a set only where every value of its items hashes by value (scalars, enums, tuples and frozen sets of them, frozen models); an array of models that hash only by identity, of Any or of containers stays a list. Deduplication and --reuse-model also keep apart models whose arrays differ in uniqueItems; without it the sets are decided before root models collapse, set item models hash by identity and such models merge, as in 0.89.0
- `--use-tuple-for-fixed-items`: Generate tuple types for arrays with items array syntax when minItems equals maxItems equals items length
- `--no-use-tuple-for-fixed-items`: Generate tuple types for arrays with items array syntax when minItems equals maxItems equals items length
- `--use-tuple-for-closed-arrays`: Generate tuple types for positional arrays that no other item can follow: a closed prefixItems tail (items, unevaluatedItems or additionalItems false) whose length the length keywords fix, so that each position keeps its own type
- `--no-use-tuple-for-closed-arrays`: Generate tuple types for positional arrays that no other item can follow: a closed prefixItems tail (items, unevaluatedItems or additionalItems false) whose length the length keywords fix, so that each position keeps its own type
- `--use-tuple-for-fixed-length-arrays`: Generate tuple types for fixed-length arrays with a single items schema
- `--use-total-false-for-typed-dict`: Generate TypedDict with total=False and mark required fields with Required
- `--use-closed-typed-dict`: Generate TypedDict with PEP 728 closed=True/extra_items for additionalProperties constraints. Use --no-use-closed-typed-dict for type checkers that don't yet support PEP 728 (e.g., mypy).
- `--no-use-closed-typed-dict`: Generate TypedDict with PEP 728 closed=True/extra_items for additionalProperties constraints. Use --no-use-closed-typed-dict for type checkers that don't yet support PEP 728 (e.g., mypy).
- `--allof-merge-mode`: Mode for field merging in allOf schemas. 'constraints': merge only constraints (minItems, maxItems, pattern, etc.) from parent (default). 'all': merge constraints plus annotations (default, examples) from parent. 'none': do not merge any fields from parent properties. Choices: `constraints`, `all`, `none`.
- `--allof-class-hierarchy`: How to map allOf references to class hierarchies. 'if-no-conflict': only create subclasses when parent class has no conflicting property definition. 'always': always create subclasses. Choices: `if-no-conflict`, `always`.
- `--use-type-alias`: Use TypeAlias instead of root models (experimental)
- `--use-type-alias-type`: Use TypeAliasType for type aliases on Python 3.10 and 3.11 (implies --use-type-alias; experimental)
- `--use-root-model-type-alias`: Use type alias format for RootModel (e.g., Foo = RootModel[Bar]) instead of class inheritance (Pydantic v2 only)
- `--use-plain-alias-for-recursive-models`: Pydantic output only: write a type alias whose whole value is a model that names itself as `Alias: TypeAlias = Node`, which Pydantic builds for every model that uses it; without it the alias is `TypeAliasType("Alias", Node)` (or `type Alias = Node`) as in 0.89.0, which Pydantic 2 refuses once two models use it. The alias then has no entry of its own in `model_json_schema()` `$defs`
- `--no-use-plain-alias-for-recursive-models`: Pydantic output only: write a type alias whose whole value is a model that names itself as `Alias: TypeAlias = Node`, which Pydantic builds for every model that uses it; without it the alias is `TypeAliasType("Alias", Node)` (or `type Alias = Node`) as in 0.89.0, which Pydantic 2 refuses once two models use it. The alias then has no entry of its own in `model_json_schema()` `$defs`
- `--disable-future-imports`: Disable __future__ imports
- `--import-overrides`: Override modules for generated imports by symbol name. Format: JSON object mapping symbols to module paths. Example: '{"TypedDict": "my_project.typing_compat", "NotRequired": "my_project.typing_compat"}'.
- `--type-mappings`: Override default type mappings. Format: "type+format=target" (e.g., "string+binary=string" to map binary format to string type) or "format=target" (e.g., "binary=string"). Can be specified multiple times.
- `--type-overrides`: Replace schema model types with custom Python types. Format: JSON object mapping model names to Python import paths. Model-level: '{"CustomType": "my_app.types.MyType"}' replaces all references. Scoped: '{"User.field": "my_app.Type"}' replaces specific field only.
- `--type-overrides-replace-whole-type`: Make every --type-overrides value of a field replace the field's whole type: a class path replaces an object map itself, as an annotation already does (dict for builtins.dict, not dict[str, dict]), and the item counts of an array and the property counts of a map it replaces stay only where the new type counts the same (a sequence its items, a mapping class its keys), with a warning otherwise; without it a class path keeps the dict of a map around the class and every override keeps those counts whatever its type, as in 0.89.0
- `--no-type-overrides-replace-whole-type`: Make every --type-overrides value of a field replace the field's whole type: a class path replaces an object map itself, as an annotation already does (dict for builtins.dict, not dict[str, dict]), and the item counts of an array and the property counts of a map it replaces stay only where the new type counts the same (a sequence its items, a mapping class its keys), with a warning otherwise; without it a class path keeps the dict of a map around the class and every override keeps those counts whatever its type, as in 0.89.0
- `--use-x-python-type-as-written`: Write a field's x-python-type as given: a union spelled Optional[...] or Union[...], such as Optional[Literal['a', 'b']], types the field as one spelled X | Y already does, and a container class compatible with the schema, such as tuple, MutableSequence or MutableMapping, is written around the schema's item, key and value types; without it such a union is ignored where the schema declares one type, and the field takes the schema's type, and such a container is written as list, Sequence, set, frozenset or Mapping, as in 0.90.0
- `--no-use-x-python-type-as-written`: Write a field's x-python-type as given: a union spelled Optional[...] or Union[...], such as Optional[Literal['a', 'b']], types the field as one spelled X | Y already does, and a container class compatible with the schema, such as tuple, MutableSequence or MutableMapping, is written around the schema's item, key and value types; without it such a union is ignored where the schema declares one type, and the field takes the schema's type, and such a container is written as list, Sequence, set, frozenset or Mapping, as in 0.90.0
- `--use-bytes-for-content-media-type`: Type a string of an OpenAPI document that has a contentMediaType and no contentEncoding as bytes, as a format: binary string is: OpenAPI 3.1 writes raw binary content so, and the generated clients and servers already send and receive it as a file; without it the string is str, as in 0.90.0
- `--no-use-bytes-for-content-media-type`: Type a string of an OpenAPI document that has a contentMediaType and no contentEncoding as bytes, as a format: binary string is: OpenAPI 3.1 writes raw binary content so, and the generated clients and servers already send and receive it as a file; without it the string is str, as in 0.90.0

## Field Customization

Field naming, aliases, defaults, and constraints.

- `--extra-fields`: Set the generated models to allow, forbid, or ignore extra fields. Choices: `allow`, `ignore`, `forbid`.
- `--use-schema-description`: Use schema description to populate class docstring
- `--no-use-schema-description`: Use schema description to populate class docstring
- `--use-title-as-name`: use titles as class names of models
- `--no-use-title-as-name`: use titles as class names of models
- `--infer-union-variant-names`: Name inline oneOf/anyOf branch models after the value of their tag field (Pet + type: "cat" -> PetCat) instead of Pet1, Pet2
- `--use-tag-as-union-variant-name`: Name inline oneOf/anyOf branch models after their tag: what --infer-union-variant-names does, skipping tags whose class names collide, plus single-branch unions (type: "exec" -> LocalShellActionExec) and single-key branches ({"granular": ...} -> AskForApprovalGranular)
- `--name-allof-union-members-after-branches`: Name the classes an allOf gives the branches of a oneOf or anyOf it holds after the branch: the holder and the branch's tag (with --infer-union-variant-names or --use-tag-as-union-variant-name), its $ref class or its position (EventCreated, or Event1), the branch-only base after the class (EventCreatedBase) and the shared part after the holder (EventBase); without it every class is numbered after the holder (Event1 to Event5), as in 0.89.0
- `--no-name-allof-union-members-after-branches`: Name the classes an allOf gives the branches of a oneOf or anyOf it holds after the branch: the holder and the branch's tag (with --infer-union-variant-names or --use-tag-as-union-variant-name), its $ref class or its position (EventCreated, or Event1), the branch-only base after the class (EventCreatedBase) and the shared part after the holder (EventBase); without it every class is numbered after the holder (Event1 to Event5), as in 0.89.0
- `--field-constraints`: Use field constraints and not con* annotations
- `--omit-redundant-constraints`: Do not write a constraint again beside a type that already enforces it: the bound of a zero-bound class such as NonNegativeInt, and the length and number constraints a const or enum Literal meets by its values
- `--no-omit-redundant-constraints`: Do not write a constraint again beside a type that already enforces it: the bound of a zero-bound class such as NonNegativeInt, and the length and number constraints a const or enum Literal meets by its values
- `--read-length-keywords-by-type`: Read minLength, maxLength and pattern for strings only and minItems, maxItems and uniqueItems for arrays only, as JSON Schema does, so a maxLength beside an array leaves the list unbounded and a maxItems beside a string leaves the string unbounded; without it a declared array writes minLength/maxLength and a declared string minItems/maxItems as their length bounds, as in 0.88.0
- `--no-read-length-keywords-by-type`: Read minLength, maxLength and pattern for strings only and minItems, maxItems and uniqueItems for arrays only, as JSON Schema does, so a maxLength beside an array leaves the list unbounded and a maxItems beside a string leaves the string unbounded; without it a declared array writes minLength/maxLength and a declared string minItems/maxItems as their length bounds, as in 0.88.0
- `--read-msgspec-union-bounds-exactly`: msgspec.Struct output only: decide whether the int member of a union with a number member drops its Meta bounds on the bounds the schema writes, exactly; without it a number member's bound past 2**53 is read as the float it is written as, so the int member can keep a bound that rejects an integer the number member accepts, as in 0.88.0
- `--no-read-msgspec-union-bounds-exactly`: msgspec.Struct output only: decide whether the int member of a union with a number member drops its Meta bounds on the bounds the schema writes, exactly; without it a number member's bound past 2**53 is read as the float it is written as, so the int member can keep a bound that rejects an integer the number member accepts, as in 0.88.0
- `--use-site-models-for-constrained-refs`: Give an allOf of $ref members whose other parts add constraints, an enum or a type its own model of the values all parts admit, instead of the referenced type, which leaves the added assertions out
- `--no-use-site-models-for-constrained-refs`: Give an allOf of $ref members whose other parts add constraints, an enum or a type its own model of the values all parts admit, instead of the referenced type, which leaves the added assertions out
- `--use-one-model-per-ref-site`: Give an object $ref with sibling keywords one model per place it is written, which every unchanged copy of that place shares, and parse such chains without nesting; without it each path that reaches the place gets a model of its own (N(N-1)/2 site models for a chain of N definitions), as in 0.89.0.
- `--no-use-one-model-per-ref-site`: Give an object $ref with sibling keywords one model per place it is written, which every unchanged copy of that place shares, and parse such chains without nesting; without it each path that reaches the place gets a model of its own (N(N-1)/2 site models for a chain of N definitions), as in 0.89.0.
- `--set-default-enum-member` (deprecated): Deprecated: --set-default-enum-member is deprecated. Use --deserialize-default-values enum instead.
- `--use-enum-values-in-discriminator`: Use enum member literals in discriminator fields instead of string literals
- `--merge-shared-variant-tags`: Give a variant that several discriminated unions tag differently (for example one by a mapping key, one by the schema name) every tag they give it, so each union decodes the documents its discriminator selects; such a union also accepts the tags the other unions give the variant. A variant keeps the tag of the first union, as without the option (as in 0.88.0), where a union listing it would then give two of its variants one tag, and msgspec Structs, which take one tag, keep it too.
- `--no-merge-shared-variant-tags`: Give a variant that several discriminated unions tag differently (for example one by a mapping key, one by the schema name) every tag they give it, so each union decodes the documents its discriminator selects; such a union also accepts the tags the other unions give the variant. A variant keeps the tag of the first union, as without the option (as in 0.88.0), where a union listing it would then give two of its variants one tag, and msgspec Structs, which take one tag, keep it too.
- `--capitalise-enum-members`: Capitalize field names on enum
- `--capitalize-enum-members`: Capitalize field names on enum
- `--capitalise-numbered-enum-members`: Under --capitalise-enum-members, capitalize also the number a member takes when its capitalized name is taken (A_1 instead of a_1 for the members 'a' and 'A'); without it the numbered name stays as written, as in 0.88.0
- `--no-capitalise-numbered-enum-members`: Under --capitalise-enum-members, capitalize also the number a member takes when its capitalized name is taken (A_1 instead of a_1 for the members 'a' and 'A'); without it the numbered name stays as written, as in 0.88.0
- `--capitalize-numbered-enum-members`: Under --capitalise-enum-members, capitalize also the number a member takes when its capitalized name is taken (A_1 instead of a_1 for the members 'a' and 'A'); without it the numbered name stays as written, as in 0.88.0
- `--no-capitalize-numbered-enum-members`: Under --capitalise-enum-members, capitalize also the number a member takes when its capitalized name is taken (A_1 instead of a_1 for the members 'a' and 'A'); without it the numbered name stays as written, as in 0.88.0
- `--empty-enum-field-name`: Set field name when enum value is empty (default: `_`)
- `--field-extra-keys`: Add extra keys to field parameters
- `--field-extra-keys-without-x-prefix`: Add extra keys with `x-` prefix to field parameters. The extra keys are stripped of the `x-` prefix.
- `--field-include-all-keys`: Add all keys to field parameters
- `--original-field-name-delimiter`: Set delimiter to convert to snake case. This option only can be used with --snake-case-field (default: `_` )
- `--remove-special-field-name-prefix`: Remove field name prefix if it has a special meaning e.g. underscores
- `--snake-case-field`: Change camel-case field name to snake-case
- `--no-snake-case-field`: Change camel-case field name to snake-case
- `--special-field-name-prefix`: Set field name prefix when first character can't be used as Python field name (default: `field`)
- `--use-field-description`: Use schema description to populate field docstring
- `--no-use-field-description`: Use schema description to populate field docstring
- `--use-field-description-example`: Use schema example to populate field docstring
- `--no-use-field-description-example`: Use schema example to populate field docstring
- `--use-attribute-docstrings`: Set use_attribute_docstrings=True in Pydantic v2 ConfigDict
- `--use-inline-field-description`: Use schema description to populate field docstring as inline docstring
- `--use-single-line-docstring`: Use single-line docstrings when the content fits on one line
- `--no-use-single-line-docstring`: Use single-line docstrings when the content fits on one line
- `--no-alias`: Do not add a field alias. E.g., if --snake-case-field is used along with a base class, which has an alias_generator
- `--use-serialization-alias`: Use serialization_alias instead of alias for field aliasing (Pydantic v2 only). This allows setting values using the Pythonic field name while serializing to the original name.
- `--serialization-aliases`: Serialization alias mapping as inline JSON or a JSON file path for Pydantic v2. Format: {'<schema_field>': '<serialization_alias>'}. Supports hierarchical formats: Flat: {'name': 'fullName'} applies to all occurrences. Scoped: {'User.name': 'fullName'} applies to specific class.
- `--field-type-collision-strategy`: Strategy for handling field name and type name collisions (Pydantic v2 only). 'rename-field': rename field with suffix and add alias (default). 'rename-type': rename type class with suffix to preserve field name. Choices: `rename-field`, `rename-type`.
- `--aliases`: Alias mapping as inline JSON or a JSON file path for renaming fields. Format: {'<schema_field>': '<python_name>'} - the schema field name becomes the Pydantic alias. Supports hierarchical formats: Flat: {'id': 'id_'} applies to all occurrences. Scoped: {'User.name': 'user_name'} applies to specific class. Priority: scoped > flat. Multiple aliases (Pydantic v2 only): {'field': ['alt1', 'alt2']} uses AliasChoices for validation. Example: {'User.name': 'user_name', 'id': 'id_'} generates `id_: ... = Field(alias='id')`.
- `--default-values`: Default value overrides as inline JSON or a JSON file path. Supports hierarchical formats: Flat: {'field': value} applies to all occurrences. Scoped: {'ClassName.field': value} applies to specific class. Priority: scoped > flat. Note: Scoped keys use the generated class name for JSON Schema/OpenAPI. Required fields remain required unless --use-default is also specified. Example: {'User.status': 'active', 'page': 1, 'limit': 10}
- `--deserialize-default-values`: Deserialize serialized schema defaults for selected generated types. Supported values: decimal, enum. Choices: `decimal`, `enum`.
- `--no-deserialize-default-values`: Disable schema default value deserialization.

## Model Customization

Generated model class and package behavior.

- `--output-model-type`: Output model type (default: pydantic_v2.BaseModel) Choices: `pydantic_v2.BaseModel`, `pydantic_v2.dataclass`, `dataclasses.dataclass`, `typing.TypedDict`, `msgspec.Struct`.
- `--allow-extra-fields` (deprecated): Deprecated: --allow-extra-fields is deprecated. Use --extra-fields=allow instead.
- `--allow-population-by-field-name`: Allow population by field name
- `--no-allow-population-by-field-name`: Allow population by field name
- `--class-name`: Set class name of root model
- `--model-name-map`: Rename generated model classes by schema ref or current generated class name using a JSON object or JSON file.
- `--allow-leading-underscore-class-name`: Allow an explicitly specified root class name to start with an underscore
- `--class-name-prefix`: Prefix to add to generated class names (e.g., 'Api' produces 'ApiUser'). Does not apply to root model when --class-name is specified.
- `--class-name-suffix`: Suffix to add to generated class names (e.g., 'Schema' produces 'UserSchema'). Does not apply to root model when --class-name is specified.
- `--class-name-affix-scope`: Scope for applying --class-name-prefix/--class-name-suffix. 'all': Apply to all classes including enums (default). 'models': Apply only to model classes. 'enums': Apply only to enum classes. Choices: `all`, `models`, `enums`.
- `--collapse-root-models`: Models generated with a root-type field will be merged into the models using that root-type model
- `--no-collapse-root-models`: Models generated with a root-type field will be merged into the models using that root-type model
- `--collapse-root-models-name-strategy`: Strategy for naming when collapsing root models that reference other models. 'child': Keep inner model's name (default). 'parent': Use wrapper's name for inner model. Requires --collapse-root-models to be set. Choices: `child`, `parent`.
- `--collapse-shared-parent-wrappers`: Under --collapse-root-models-name-strategy parent, make every model that references a wrapper reference the inner model that takes its name, as its first model does; without it, where --field-type-collision-strategy rename-type can rename the wrapper apart from the inner model in their module, the later models keep the wrapper
- `--no-collapse-shared-parent-wrappers`: Under --collapse-root-models-name-strategy parent, make every model that references a wrapper reference the inner model that takes its name, as its first model does; without it, where --field-type-collision-strategy rename-type can rename the wrapper apart from the inner model in their module, the later models keep the wrapper
- `--keep-constrained-root-models-in-every-container`: Under --collapse-root-models with --field-constraints, keep a root model whose root field has constraints named inside any container of its holder, a set, frozen set, Sequence or Mapping as well as a list, dict or union, as `Field()` could not carry them there; without it such a root model is inlined into those containers and its constraints are lost, as in 0.89.0
- `--no-keep-constrained-root-models-in-every-container`: Under --collapse-root-models with --field-constraints, keep a root model whose root field has constraints named inside any container of its holder, a set, frozen set, Sequence or Mapping as well as a list, dict or union, as `Field()` could not carry them there; without it such a root model is inlined into those containers and its constraints are lost, as in 0.89.0
- `--keep-enum-literal-aliases`: Under --collapse-root-models, keep a named enum that the output writes as a `Literal` type alias named at its uses (`Status = Literal['open', 'resolved']`, `a: Status`); without it every use repeats the `Literal`, as in 0.89.0
- `--no-keep-enum-literal-aliases`: Under --collapse-root-models, keep a named enum that the output writes as a `Literal` type alias named at its uses (`Status = Literal['open', 'resolved']`, `a: Status`); without it every use repeats the `Literal`, as in 0.89.0
- `--keep-reference-null-on-collapsed-root-models`: Under --collapse-root-models, keep the null of a root model that admits null where a field, item or map value that names it takes its type (an OpenAPI 3.0 `nullable: true` root: `list[str] | None`), as the root model admits it; without it the inlined type rejects null, as in 0.89.0
- `--no-keep-reference-null-on-collapsed-root-models`: Under --collapse-root-models, keep the null of a root model that admits null where a field, item or map value that names it takes its type (an OpenAPI 3.0 `nullable: true` root: `list[str] | None`), as the root model admits it; without it the inlined type rejects null, as in 0.89.0
- `--keep-shared-members-on-collapsed-root-models`: Under --collapse-root-models, keep each member of a root type that collapse inlined at several sites at every site when a root model that member names is collapsed later, as a recursive union reaches its plain member (`dict[str, Union["Entry", str]]`); without it those sites write the union without that member, or `Any` where no member is left, as in 0.90.0
- `--no-keep-shared-members-on-collapsed-root-models`: Under --collapse-root-models, keep each member of a root type that collapse inlined at several sites at every site when a root model that member names is collapsed later, as a recursive union reaches its plain member (`dict[str, Union["Entry", str]]`); without it those sites write the union without that member, or `Any` where no member is left, as in 0.90.0
- `--collapse-constrained-root-models-as-annotated`: Under --collapse-root-models with --use-annotated, inline a root model of a string with constraints into the union, list, dict or other container of its holder as `Annotated[str, Field(...)]`, which keeps the constraints on that member; without it such a root model stays named there, as in 0.90.0
- `--no-collapse-constrained-root-models-as-annotated`: Under --collapse-root-models with --use-annotated, inline a root model of a string with constraints into the union, list, dict or other container of its holder as `Annotated[str, Field(...)]`, which keeps the constraints on that member; without it such a root model stays named there, as in 0.90.0
- `--remove-unused-models-beside-type-overrides`: Remove the models that nothing uses, such as a root model --collapse-root-models inlined, also from a module a model-level --type-overrides key takes a model out of, as from every other module; without it they stay written there, as in 0.90.0
- `--no-remove-unused-models-beside-type-overrides`: Remove the models that nothing uses, such as a root model --collapse-root-models inlined, also from a module a model-level --type-overrides key takes a model out of, as from every other module; without it they stay written there, as in 0.90.0
- `--keep-self-referencing-array-items`: Keep the items of an array whose items name the array itself (`Node = array of Node | Leaf`: `RootModel[list[Node | Leaf]]`), and serialize the root of a type list that lists such an array as any subclass under --use-serialize-as-any; msgspec output, which cannot decode such a type alias, keeps the bare `list`; without it the array is written as a bare `list`, as in 0.90.0
- `--no-keep-self-referencing-array-items`: Keep the items of an array whose items name the array itself (`Node = array of Node | Leaf`: `RootModel[list[Node | Leaf]]`), and serialize the root of a type list that lists such an array as any subclass under --use-serialize-as-any; msgspec output, which cannot decode such a type alias, keeps the bare `list`; without it the array is written as a bare `list`, as in 0.90.0
- `--collapse-reuse-models`: When used with --reuse-model, collapse duplicate models by replacing references instead of creating empty inheritance subclasses. This eliminates 'class Foo(Bar): pass' patterns
- `--no-collapse-reuse-models`: When used with --reuse-model, collapse duplicate models by replacing references instead of creating empty inheritance subclasses. This eliminates 'class Foo(Bar): pass' patterns
- `--skip-root-model`: Skip generating the model for the root schema element
- `--use-root-model-sequence-interface`: Make non-null sequence-like Pydantic v2 RootModel classes implement collections.abc.Sequence by adding Sequence[T] inheritance and root-delegating __iter__, __getitem__, and __len__ methods
- `--singularize-last-word-of-item-names`: Name the item model of an array by singularizing only the last word of its name (actions_caches gives ActionsCache, payment_status gives PaymentStatusItem); without it the whole name is singularized as one word (ActionsCach, PaymentStatu), as in 0.88.0
- `--no-singularize-last-word-of-item-names`: Name the item model of an array by singularizing only the last word of its name (actions_caches gives ActionsCache, payment_status gives PaymentStatusItem); without it the whole name is singularized as one word (ActionsCach, PaymentStatu), as in 0.88.0
- `--enable-faux-immutability`: Enable faux immutability
- `--keep-model-order`: Keep generated models' order
- `--order-constructor-fields-by`: Decide the order of constructor fields by each given value. final-names: order the constructor fields of dataclass and msgspec.Struct models after every field has its final name, so a field that overrides an inherited field renamed in another module is matched to it and keeps its place; without it the override reads as a new field after the inherited default and is written keyword-only (kw_only=True). written-defaults: order the fields of msgspec.Struct and Pydantic dataclass models by the defaults they write, so under --strip-default-none an optional field whose None default is stripped but still written (UNSET, or None for a type that admits None) goes after the required fields of a Struct with the other optional fields and stays positional after an inherited default, and a required pydantic.dataclass field redeclaring it is written Field(...) (a msgspec.Struct writes a bare annotation); without it the field keeps its place among the fields without a default, as before: it is keyword-only after an inherited default, a redeclaring field inherits its None default, and the fields are reordered only where a required field would then follow a default. Choices: `final-names`, `written-defaults`.
- `--keyword-only`: Defined models as keyword only (for example dataclass(kw_only=True)).
- `--frozen-dataclasses`: Generate frozen dataclasses (dataclass(frozen=True)). Only applies to dataclass output.
- `--dataclass-arguments`: Custom dataclass arguments as a JSON dictionary, e.g. '{"frozen": true, "kw_only": true}'. Overrides --frozen-dataclasses and similar flags.
- `--keep-false-dataclass-arguments`: Write every dataclass decorator argument set to false, such as eq=False from --dataclass-arguments '{"eq": false}', so the dataclass compares by identity as asked; without it an argument set to false is left out and takes its default (eq=True), as in 0.89.0
- `--no-keep-false-dataclass-arguments`: Write every dataclass decorator argument set to false, such as eq=False from --dataclass-arguments '{"eq": false}', so the dataclass compares by identity as asked; without it an argument set to false is left out and takes its default (eq=True), as in 0.89.0
- `--use-msgspec-tagged-unions`: msgspec.Struct output only: write a discriminated union as msgspec tagged structs as a whole. Every variant is tagged with the document's property name and its value, or none is and a warning says why. Without it the 0.83.0 form is kept, which tags only a variant whose discriminator is a single literal and keeps the other discriminators as Literal fields.
- `--tag-msgspec-by-payload-name`: msgspec.Struct output only: tag the structs of a discriminated union with the property name the document carries (for example 'pet-kind') instead of the Python name that property resolves to (pet_kind), which msgspec looks for in the payload. --use-msgspec-tagged-unions already tags by the document's property name. Without either option the Python name is kept.
- `--no-tag-msgspec-by-payload-name`: msgspec.Struct output only: tag the structs of a discriminated union with the property name the document carries (for example 'pet-kind') instead of the Python name that property resolves to (pet_kind), which msgspec looks for in the payload. --use-msgspec-tagged-unions already tags by the document's property name. Without either option the Python name is kept.
- `--use-msgspec-meta-for-map-keys`: msgspec.Struct output only: write the keys of a map whose keys propertyNames or patternProperties constrain by pattern, minLength or maxLength as Annotated[str, Meta(...)], so msgspec checks them as Pydantic output does; without it the keys are str and every key is accepted, as in 0.88.0
- `--no-use-msgspec-meta-for-map-keys`: msgspec.Struct output only: write the keys of a map whose keys propertyNames or patternProperties constrain by pattern, minLength or maxLength as Annotated[str, Meta(...)], so msgspec checks them as Pydantic output does; without it the keys are str and every key is accepted, as in 0.88.0
- `--use-msgspec-forbid-unknown-fields`: msgspec.Struct output only: write forbid_unknown_fields=True on a Struct whose schema admits no property but its own (additionalProperties: false without patternProperties beside it, also in an inline allOf member, or unevaluatedProperties: false in an inline allOf member), so msgspec rejects the unknown fields the schema rejects, as Pydantic output does with extra='forbid'; --extra-fields forbid writes it on every Struct, also without --use-generic-base-class, and --extra-fields allow or ignore and --allow-extra-fields keep it open. Without it such a Struct ignores unknown fields, as in 0.89.0
- `--no-use-msgspec-forbid-unknown-fields`: msgspec.Struct output only: write forbid_unknown_fields=True on a Struct whose schema admits no property but its own (additionalProperties: false without patternProperties beside it, also in an inline allOf member, or unevaluatedProperties: false in an inline allOf member), so msgspec rejects the unknown fields the schema rejects, as Pydantic output does with extra='forbid'; --extra-fields forbid writes it on every Struct, also without --use-generic-base-class, and --extra-fields allow or ignore and --allow-extra-fields keep it open. Without it such a Struct ignores unknown fields, as in 0.89.0
- `--use-msgspec-nullable-enum-alias`: msgspec.Struct output only: write an enum that lists null as an Enum without the None member plus an Enum | None type alias, so that msgspec can decode it. Without it a plain Enum keeps the 0.83.0 None member, which msgspec cannot decode; an IntEnum or --use-subclass-enum enum, which cannot hold it, is written without it and, as its one type rejects null, without the alias.
- `--reuse-model`: Reuse models on the field when a module has the model with the same content
- `--no-reuse-model`: Reuse models on the field when a module has the model with the same content
- `--reuse-scope`: Scope for model reuse deduplication: module (per-file, default) or tree (cross-file with shared module). Only effective when --reuse-model is set. Choices: `module`, `tree`.
- `--target-python-version`: target python version Choices: `3.10`, `3.11`, `3.12`, `3.13`, `3.14`, `3.15`.
- `--target-pydantic-version`: Oldest Pydantic version the generated code must support. Unset: the newest supported feature forms, with populate_by_name config like '2' and the experimental MISSING import like '2.12'. '2': Pydantic 2.0.3+ compatible (uses populate_by_name; patterns that need Python's regex engine need 2.5+). '2.11': Pydantic 2.11+ (uses validate_by_name). '2.12': Pydantic 2.12+ (supports MISSING sentinel). '2.14': Pydantic 2.14+ (imports MISSING from pydantic; bytes patterns can select Python's regex engine; pydantic_v2.dataclass writes required Field(...) fields before the fields with defaults of the same class; a number schema keeps multipleOf on a timedelta). Constructs without an older form are written for every target, with a warning naming the Pydantic they need. Choices: `2`, `2.11`, `2.12`, `2.14`.
- `--alias-generator`: Pydantic v2 BaseModel alias generator to use in ConfigDict. Matching generated aliases are omitted from individual Field() calls, except with --target-pydantic-version 2, which writes every alias. Choices: `to_camel`, `to_pascal`, `to_snake`.
- `--pin-aliases-with-alias-generator`: pydantic_v2.BaseModel and pydantic_v2.dataclass output: decide a field's alias by the alias generator its model applies, the one in its config or in the config it inherits. For a dataclass and a --target-pydantic-version older than 2.8, whose alias generators can differ from the generated aliases, write the generated alias on every field of a dataclass whose config names an alias generator. Without it a field keeps the alias it has without the generator, which the config then replaces.
- `--no-pin-aliases-with-alias-generator`: pydantic_v2.BaseModel and pydantic_v2.dataclass output: decide a field's alias by the alias generator its model applies, the one in its config or in the config it inherits. For a dataclass and a --target-pydantic-version older than 2.8, whose alias generators can differ from the generated aliases, write the generated alias on every field of a dataclass whose config names an alias generator. Without it a field keeps the alias it has without the generator, which the config then replaces.
- `--use-generic-base-class`: Generate a shared base class with model configuration (e.g., extra='forbid') instead of repeating the configuration in each model. Keeps code DRY.
- `--parent-scoped-naming` (deprecated): Deprecated: --parent-scoped-naming is deprecated. Use --naming-strategy parent-prefixed instead.
- `--naming-strategy`: Strategy for naming models and telling duplicate model names apart. 'numbered' (default): Append numeric suffix (Address, Address1, Address2). Simple but names don't indicate context. 'parent-prefixed': Prefix every nested model with the name of the model that holds it, joined in CamelCase, nested parents included (CompanyAddress, CompanyEmployeeHomeAddress), also where the name is unique; the model names are the same as with 'full-path'. 'full-path': Prefix every nested model with the names of the models that hold it, joined in CamelCase (CompanyAddress, CompanyEmployeeHomeAddress). 'primary-first': Keep clean names for primary definitions (in /definitions/ or /components/schemas/), only add suffix to inline/nested duplicates. 'definitions-first': Give every definition (in /definitions/, /$defs/ or /components/schemas/ of any document) its own name before an inline model, a variant or another definition that asked for it first, which takes the name the definition would have taken (Package1); unlike 'primary-first', which renames only models of other files, as in 0.89.0. 'enclosing-model': Prefix every nested model with the final name of the model it is built for, once (IssueClosedIssue for the allOf property issue of IssueClosed, StreamEvent1 for the first unnamed branch of the union StreamEvent, PetCat for its branch tagged cat); a definition keeps its own name (Customer, not ModelCustomer); unlike 'full-path', which prefixes with the closest model registered above, as in 0.89.0. Choices: `numbered`, `parent-prefixed`, `full-path`, `primary-first`, `definitions-first`, `enclosing-model`.
- `--duplicate-name-suffix`: JSON mapping of type to suffix for resolving duplicate name conflicts. Example: '{"model": "Schema"}' changes Address1 to AddressSchema. Keys: 'model' (for classes), 'enum' (for enums), 'default' (fallback). When not specified, uses numeric suffix (Address1, Address2).
- `--use-duplicate-name-suffix-for-every-collision`: Give the --duplicate-name-suffix suffix also to a model renamed because its name is taken in its module, by another model or by a name the module imports (an inline Item beside a definition Item, a definition AnyUrl beside a uri field); without it such a model takes the suffix Model, as in 0.88.0
- `--no-use-duplicate-name-suffix-for-every-collision`: Give the --duplicate-name-suffix suffix also to a model renamed because its name is taken in its module, by another model or by a name the module imports (an inline Item beside a definition Item, a definition AnyUrl beside a uri field); without it such a model takes the suffix Model, as in 0.88.0
- `--name-converted-payloads-by-message`: AsyncAPI only: name a payload that an Avro or XML Schema converter gives no name of its own, such as an Avro string or array, after its message, as a JSON Schema payload is, and drop the placeholder title Model the converter gives it (Field(..., title='Model'), and the class Model under --use-title-as-name); without it the placeholder stays, as in 0.88.0
- `--no-name-converted-payloads-by-message`: AsyncAPI only: name a payload that an Avro or XML Schema converter gives no name of its own, such as an Avro string or array, after its message, as a JSON Schema payload is, and drop the placeholder title Model the converter gives it (Field(..., title='Model'), and the class Model under --use-title-as-name); without it the placeholder stays, as in 0.88.0
- `--base-class`: Base Class (default: pydantic.BaseModel)
- `--base-class-map`: Model-specific base class mapping (JSON or JSON file path). Example: '{"MyModel": "custom.BaseA", "OtherModel": "custom.BaseB"}'. Priority: base-class-map > customBasePath (in schema) > base-class.
- `--use-serialize-as-any`: Use pydantic.SerializeAsAny for fields with types that have subtypes (Pydantic v2 only)
- `--use-serialize-as-any-for-every-subclass`: Under --use-serialize-as-any, wrap a field in SerializeAsAny when any subclass of its model in the generated output adds fields: at any depth, after --reuse-model or --collapse-reuse-models merges the model, and where the field names the model through its module; without it only a field whose model has a direct subclass is wrapped, as in 0.88.0 (Pydantic v2 only)
- `--no-use-serialize-as-any-for-every-subclass`: Under --use-serialize-as-any, wrap a field in SerializeAsAny when any subclass of its model in the generated output adds fields: at any depth, after --reuse-model or --collapse-reuse-models merges the model, and where the field names the model through its module; without it only a field whose model has a direct subclass is wrapped, as in 0.88.0 (Pydantic v2 only)
- `--use-one-literal-as-default`: Use one literal as default value for one literal field
- `--use-subclass-enum`: Define generic Enum class as subclass with field type when enum has type (int, float, bytes, str)
- `--no-use-subclass-enum`: Define generic Enum class as subclass with field type when enum has type (int, float, bytes, str)
- `--model-extra-keys`: Add extra keys from schema extensions (x-* fields) to model_config json_schema_extra
- `--model-extra-keys-without-x-prefix`: Add extra keys with `x-` prefix to model_config json_schema_extra. The extra keys are stripped of the `x-` prefix.
- `--force-optional`: Force optional for required fields
- `--strict-nullable`: Treat default field as a non-nullable field
- `--no-strict-nullable`: Treat default field as a non-nullable field
- `--omit-redundant-reference-null`: Do not write None again where a field, item or member references a model that holds null itself (a root model or type alias whose type admits None, or an enum with a None member), so that a null parses to that model
- `--no-omit-redundant-reference-null`: Do not write None again where a field, item or member references a model that holds null itself (a root model or type alias whose type admits None, or an enum with a None member), so that a null parses to that model
- `--keep-reference-null-on-merged-models`: Keep the null that the schema of a field, item or member admits where the model it references is merged into an equal model that rejects null (deduplication of equal models, --reuse-model, --collapse-reuse-models, --reuse-scope tree), so a `type: [object, null]` property keeps `| None`; without it the reference takes the null of the model it names after the merge, as in 0.88.0
- `--no-keep-reference-null-on-merged-models`: Keep the null that the schema of a field, item or member admits where the model it references is merged into an equal model that rejects null (deduplication of equal models, --reuse-model, --collapse-reuse-models, --reuse-scope tree), so a `type: [object, null]` property keeps `| None`; without it the reference takes the null of the model it names after the merge, as in 0.88.0
- `--strip-default-none`: Strip default None on fields (no effect on msgspec.Struct: it defaults an omitted field to UNSET, and to None only when the type admits None)
- `--use-default`: Use default value even if a field is required
- `--use-default-kwarg`: Use `default=` instead of a positional argument for Fields that have default values.
- `--no-use-default-kwarg`: Use `default=` instead of a positional argument for Fields that have default values.
- `--apply-field-options-to-every-field`: Apply the field options to every kind of field: a GraphQL field, a property whose schema is `true` or `false`, a required name without a property and the tag field a discriminator appends take the field options the other fields take, such as --use-default-kwarg, --use-annotated and --use-default-factory-for-optional-nested-models; without it they leave them out, as in 0.90.0
- `--no-apply-field-options-to-every-field`: Apply the field options to every kind of field: a GraphQL field, a property whose schema is `true` or `false`, a required name without a property and the tag field a discriminator appends take the field options the other fields take, such as --use-default-kwarg, --use-annotated and --use-default-factory-for-optional-nested-models; without it they leave them out, as in 0.90.0
- `--use-missing-sentinel`: Use pydantic.experimental.missing_sentinel.MISSING for optional fields without defaults (Pydantic v2.12+), or pydantic.MISSING with --target-pydantic-version 2.14 or later, which --generate-server and --generate-client require with this option. Supports pydantic_v2.BaseModel and pydantic_v2.dataclass, whose server and client generation requires it.
- `--read-nullable-beside-type-list`: Write the null that `nullable: true` declares beside a `type` list with an object into the root model of that schema under --strict-nullable or --use-missing-sentinel, as a declared field does; without it only a `type` list holding null makes that root admit None
- `--no-read-nullable-beside-type-list`: Write the null that `nullable: true` declares beside a `type` list with an object into the root model of that schema under --strict-nullable or --use-missing-sentinel, as a declared field does; without it only a `type` list holding null makes that root admit None
- `--keep-field-defaults-off-branch-roots`: Leave the default of a property off the root models extracted from the branches of its `anyOf` or `oneOf`, which then require their value; without it each such root takes the property's default
- `--no-keep-field-defaults-off-branch-roots`: Leave the default of a property off the root models extracted from the branches of its `anyOf` or `oneOf`, which then require their value; without it each such root takes the property's default
- `--union-mode`: Union mode for only pydantic v2 field Choices: `smart`, `left_to_right`.
- `--use-frozen-field`: Use Field(frozen=True) for readOnly fields (Pydantic v2).
- `--no-use-frozen-field`: Use Field(frozen=True) for readOnly fields (Pydantic v2).
- `--use-default-factory-for-optional-nested-models`: Use default_factory for optional nested model fields instead of None default. E.g., `field: Model | None = Field(default_factory=Model)` instead of `field: Model | None = None`

## Template Customization

Formatting, custom templates, and generated file headers.

- `--disable-appending-item-suffix`: Disable appending `Item` suffix to model name in an array
- `--disable-timestamp`: Disable timestamp on file headers
- `--no-disable-timestamp`: Disable timestamp on file headers
- `--enable-version-header`: Enable package version on file headers
- `--enable-command-header`: Enable command-line options on file headers for reproducibility
- `--enable-generated-header-marker`: Enable @generated marker on file headers
- `--treat-dot-as-module`: Treat dotted schema names as module paths, creating nested directory structures (e.g., 'foo.bar.Model' becomes 'foo/bar.py'). Use --no-treat-dot-as-module to keep dots in names as underscores for single-file output.
- `--no-treat-dot-as-module`: Treat dotted schema names as module paths, creating nested directory structures (e.g., 'foo.bar.Model' becomes 'foo/bar.py'). Use --no-treat-dot-as-module to keep dots in names as underscores for single-file output.
- `--strict-dotted-module-names`: Only infer dotted schema names as module paths when every segment is a canonical Python identifier. This applies only to automatic inference and does not override --treat-dot-as-module or --no-treat-dot-as-module.
- `--no-strict-dotted-module-names`: Only infer dotted schema names as module paths when every segment is a canonical Python identifier. This applies only to automatic inference and does not override --treat-dot-as-module or --no-treat-dot-as-module.
- `--rename-submodules-hidden-by-classes`: Rename a submodule named like a class of its package, such as pkg/Warn.py beside the class Warn of pkg/__init__.py, to the first free name with trailing underscores (pkg/Warn_.py), with the modules below it; the class keeps its name. Without it importing the submodule replaces the class in its package, so the models that use either fail to decode
- `--no-rename-submodules-hidden-by-classes`: Rename a submodule named like a class of its package, such as pkg/Warn.py beside the class Warn of pkg/__init__.py, to the first free name with trailing underscores (pkg/Warn_.py), with the modules below it; the class keeps its name. Without it importing the submodule replaces the class in its package, so the models that use either fail to decode
- `--use-exact-imports`: import exact types instead of modules, for example: "from .foo import Bar" instead of "from . import foo" with "foo.Bar"
- `--custom-file-header`: Custom file header
- `--custom-file-header-path`: Custom file header file path
- `--custom-file-header-mode`: How to combine a custom file header with the generated header (default: replace) Choices: `replace`, `prepend`.
- `--custom-template-dir`: Custom template directory
- `--extra-template-data`: Extra template data for output models as inline JSON or a JSON file path. For OpenAPI and Jsonschema the keys are the spec path of the object, or the name of the object if you want to apply the template data to multiple objects with the same name. If you are using another input file type (e.g. GraphQL), the key is the name of the object. The value is a dictionary of the template data to add.
- `--validators`: Validators configuration as inline JSON or a JSON file path. Defines field validators for Pydantic v2 models. Keys are model names, values contain validator definitions with field, function, and mode.
- `--generate-schema-validators`: Generate Pydantic v2 model validators for JSON Schema rules that cannot be represented as type hints (experimental).
- `--check-pattern-maps-strictly`: Under --generate-schema-validators, count every key that a pattern of patternProperties admits, check declared keys against the patterns that match them, and keep the propertyNames keys and the other types of a type array of an object without properties
- `--no-check-pattern-maps-strictly`: Under --generate-schema-validators, count every key that a pattern of patternProperties admits, check declared keys against the patterns that match them, and keep the propertyNames keys and the other types of a type array of an object without properties
- `--schema-validator-type`: Select the schema-derived runtime validator backend. 'pydantic-v2' generates Pydantic v2 model validators (experimental). Choices: `pydantic-v2`.
- `--schema-validator-base-class-name`: Set the generated shared Pydantic v2 schema runtime validator base class name.
- `--use-type-checking-imports`: Allow Ruff to move typing-only imports into TYPE_CHECKING blocks. By default this stays enabled, except for multi-module Ruff formatting of modular Pydantic output where referenced models stay imported at runtime. Use --no-use-type-checking-imports to force runtime imports.
- `--no-use-type-checking-imports`: Allow Ruff to move typing-only imports into TYPE_CHECKING blocks. By default this stays enabled, except for multi-module Ruff formatting of modular Pydantic output where referenced models stay imported at runtime. Use --no-use-type-checking-imports to force runtime imports.
- `--use-double-quotes`: Model generated with double quotes. Single quotes or your black config skip_string_normalization value will be used without this option.
- `--wrap-string-literal`: Wrap string literal by using black `experimental-string-processing` option (require black 20.8b0 or later)
- `--additional-imports`: Custom imports for output (delimited list input). For example "datetime.date,datetime.datetime"
- `--class-decorators`: Custom decorators for generated model classes (delimited list input). For example "@dataclass_json(letter_case=LetterCase.CAMEL)". The "@" prefix is optional and will be added automatically if missing.
- `--formatters`: Formatters (current default: black, isort; future default: builtin).
